items.t: Heyo! OP here from the Prince and Villainess post, because I saw you were wrestling with yourself a bit in the tags. If it helps, while I’m aware of the Disney Descendants movies, they were also waaaaaay after my time when it comes to Disney Channel. The post was indeed inspired by something, but it was actually the “Okay, but do you deserve a big-tiddy goth girlfriend?” semi-joke that was going around tumblr a few years back. And I’ve always been into fairy tales, fantasy, and hero-villain couples. So I decided to grab the golden retriever boyfriend from other posts, set him up with the big-tiddy goth girl, and slap it all in a fairy tale land vaguely similar to The Enchanted Forest quartet by Patricia C. Wrede (fantastic read, btw, if anyone’s interested). It’s a common sentiment that there’s nothing original left in the world, no truly new ideas or stories left. I see a lot of storytellers for all forms of media get understandably frustrated by this sentiment. Personally, I actually like it quite a lot. It frees me from the pressure and expectation of having to be ‘original,’ allowing me instead to fling myself whole-hearted into whatever I actually want to write. As long as I’m not plagiarizing, who cares if someone’s told this story before? This is my take on the idea, and that’s what makes it special, not the fact that no one’s ever had this idea before. So yeah. Disney’s Descendants has similar themes. So do Ever After High, Batman/Catwoman stories, and tumblr’s very own Malfina and Connecticut Clark, along with I’m sure plenty of other stories. Because not everyone is going to enjoy all of these variations on the theme, and that’s okay. That’s why having multiple versions is a feature of the writing world as a whole, not a bug. Anyway, you don’t have to reply to this or anything, but I hope this helps with the frustration. Trust me, I’ve been there as well. And I’m sure you’ll figure out an answer to your frustrations with this topic one way or another. ;)
